description: Somos a equipe Avengers e estamos prontos para usar a tecnologia e os dados abertos da NASA para gerar impacto real no nosso planeta! O nosso foco principal é o desafio "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!", onde pretendemos analisar grandes volumes de dados ambientais, detetar padrões climáticos cruciais e transformar estatísticas complexas em insights visuais claros
summary: Trends of the Amazon is a web app that turns NASA data into clear answers about change in the Amazon basin. A user picks a question or a variable (temperature, rain, soil moisture, evapotranspiration, smoke) and the app answers four things: what is changing, where, how fast, and whether the change is statistically real. It removes the seasonal cycle, estimates the rate with a robust Theil-Sen slope, tests it with Mann-Kendall corrected for autocorrelation, and shows a 95% confidence range. It also warns when a result depends on the last few years or when a series changes direction. A map tab lets anyone query live NASA POWER data for a chosen spot. The app speaks plainly to students aged 15 to 25 and is honest about uncertainty, including when there is no clear trend. It lowers the technical barrier to investigating how a vital ecosystem is changing.
details:
What it does. The app analyses monthly NASA time series for the Amazon basin (2000 to 2025): air temperature, precipitation, evapotranspiration, soil moisture and a smoke indicator (organic carbon aerosol). For each variable it removes the seasonal cycle, estimates the rate of change per decade (Theil-Sen), tests significance (Mann-Kendall with autocorrelation correction) and shows a 95% confidence range widened by the same correction. Results are explained in plain language with a simple verdict: real trend, a hint, or nothing clear.

What makes it different. It re-runs each analysis ending in earlier years and warns when the verdict depends on the last few years. It flags series that change direction, and it can filter by season, because a variable can change in one season and not in another. A Compare tab shows how two variables move together. A Map tab lets users choose an Amazon location or type their own coordinates and see live NASA POWER data.

Impact. Many people cannot tell whether a trend is “real”. The app lowers that barrier for students and curious citizens and teaches that “no clear trend” is also a result.

Tools. Python, Streamlit, pandas, NumPy, SciPy, Plotly, NASA Giovanni (CSV exports), NASA POWER API, GitHub. Built with AI assistance (Claude, by Anthropic), see the SI section.

Factors we considered. Several datasets are model-based (MERRA-2, GLDAS) and are not independent measurements; correlation is not causation; the method estimates only linear trends; NASA POWER describes a grid cell, not an exact point. The app states these limits.
